title: SLO-driven benchmark blueprint and sample catalog
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines a reproducible SLO-driven benchmarking blueprint for the serving runtime and a compact sample catalog of benchmark scenarios used for performance acceptance, regression detection, and cost/latency trade-off analysis. It ties SLOs through to workload shapes, kernel-scheduling knobs, profiling routes, and an operational triage runbook. The goal is to produce benchmarks that are actionable for product, runtime, and infra teams: deterministic, parameterized, and traceable back to customer-facing SLOs.

Goals and scope
----------------
- Provide a repeatable benchmark design that maps to customer-facing SLOs (latency P95/P99, throughput, error-rate).
- Make benchmark inputs and provenance auditable: seed, model commit id, quantization profile, hardware SKU, runtime image tag, and runtime flags.
- Define a small catalog of representative workload shapes to cover common production patterns (short-chat, long-completion, streaming, embedding bursts, reranking).
- Include profiling/playbook steps and kernel-scheduler knobs to vary for sensitivity analysis.
- Deliver an actionable runbook for triaging regressions discovered by the benchmark suite.

SLO -> Benchmark mapping (principles)
-------------------------------------
1) Identify the SLO type and the operational target. Example SLOs we use as anchors:
   - Hosted text-generation P95 latency <= 120 ms for short-chat (seq_len <= 64) at 1.0 tokens/s request arrival per client.
   - Dedicated P99 tail latency <= 500 ms for batch inference (avg batch_size <= 8, seq_len <= 256).
   - Embeddings throughput >= 10k vectors/min with median latency <= 50 ms per vector.
   - Availability (service-level) >= 99.95% over rolling 30d.

2) For each SLO, pick a canonical workload shape and a stress envelope (light, nominal, burst, sustained).

3) Ensure benchmarks capture both steady-state and warm-start cold-path behaviors (cached KV hits vs cache-miss).

Benchmark catalog (sample scenarios)
----------------------------------
Columns: Scenario | SLO anchor | Model/variant | HW target | Load profile | Key knobs to vary
- Short-chat-interactive | P95 <= 120 ms | gpt-small-quant8-v2 | A10G | Poisson 12 rps, seq=32 | batch_linger_ms, small_batch_threshold, kv_prefetch=on
- Long-completion-burst | P99 <= 500 ms | gpt-medium-fp16 | A100-40GB | Burst 200 rps for 30s, seq=512 | dynamic_batching_enabled, kv_eviction_window
- Embedding-bulk-stream | median <= 50 ms | embed-base-quant | T4 | Steady 5k/sec | cpu_offload, async_io=on
- Rerank-low-latency | P95 <= 150 ms | rerank-compact | A10G | Concurrent 200 small requests | per_request_kernel_hint, intra_request_parallelism=1
- Mixed-tenant-preserve-slos | multiple | mixed-model-pool | heterogeneous (A10G + A100) | Multi-tenant synthetic mix | scheduler_priority_profile, quota_slotting

Workload generation recipes (examples)
-------------------------------------
1) Short-chat (interactive) generator (local):
   - CLI: ./tools/benchmark-runner --profile short-chat --model gpt-small-quant8-v2 --hw a10g --rps 12 --seq 32 --duration 600 --seed 4832
   - Trace provenance must include: git_commit=abc123def, model_sha256=f9b8..., quant_profile=q8fast_v2, runtime_flag=--use-prefetch-kv

2) Long-completion (burst) generator (k8s job):
   - Run as a k8s batch job using the official benchmark image and args --profile long-completion --duration 30 --burst-rps 200 --seq 512.

Kernel scheduling & runtime knobs to include in experiments
-----------------------------------------------------------
- batch_linger_ms: latency vs throughput tradeoff for batching. Sweep: 0, 5, 10, 20 ms.
- small_batch_threshold: when to force small-batch fast-path. Sweep: 1, 4, 8.
- per_request_kernel_hint: explicit kernel selection (fast, compact, quant). Toggle to measure accuracy vs latency.
- scheduler_priority_profile: tenant-aware profiles (background, throughput-first, latency-first).
- kv_prefetch: on/off to simulate prewarmed sessions; measure kvcache hit-rate delta.
- num_kernel_workers: controls intra-GPU concurrency; typical range 1..8 per physical device.

Profiling playbook for benchmark runs
-----------------------------------
Follow these steps when a benchmark deviates from baseline beyond defined thresholds:
1) Reproduce with exact provenance: model SHA, runtime image tag, hardware SKU and seed. Add --trace-id to correlate traces.
2) Collect traces: distributed traces, kernel timeline (nvprof / rocprof), runtime logs, and perf counters.
3) For P95 regression: check batch-size distribution, kernel selection logs, and KV cache hit-rate.
4) For P99 / tail regression: capture live kernel queue lengths, preemption counts, and scheduler backpressure metrics.
5) Memory checks: inspect allocation spikes and device OOM logs.
6) Attach profiler flamegraphs and annotate with request provenance for postmortem.

Observability and metrics (required)
-----------------------------------
- latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99 per model and per route
- request_rate (rps) by scenario and tenant
- batch_size_distribution (histogram and percentiles)
- kvcache_hit_rate and kvcache_miss_cost_ms
- gpu_utilization, sm_efficiency, memory_used_mb per device
- kernel_queue_length, preemptions_per_sec, kernel_execution_time_ms
- error_rate (5xx / timeout) and grpc_retries
- run_provenance: model_sha, runtime_image, hardware_sku, seed_id, commit_id

Alert thresholds (examples)
-------------------------
- short-chat: P95 > 140 ms (alert) / > 180 ms (page)
- long-completion: P99 > 600 ms (alert) / > 900 ms (page)
- gpu_utilization > 95% sustained for 10m -> investigate contention (may be expected)
- kvcache_hit_rate < 0.60 during warm-start suite -> alert for cache warmup regression

Runbook: triage flow for a failing benchmark
-------------------------------------------
1) Confirm provenance and re-run the scenario in an isolated single-tenant reservation.
2) Enable tracing collectors (--trace-transport=jaeger --nvprof=true) and follow the profiling playbook.
3) Quick checks (under 10 minutes):
   - Was there a model or runtime image roll? Inspect run_provenance.
   - Did batch sizes shift or show increased variance?
   - Did kernel selection move to a slower path?
4) If kernel-scheduler regression suspected: revert scheduler config to last-known-good and rerun.
5) Open an incident sized by SLO impact and notify runtime-kernel owners with links to traces and profiling artifacts.

Release gating and CI integration
--------------------------------
- Every runtime release must pass nominal and warm-start benchmarks on A10G and A100-40GB before canary promotion.
- Performance regressions > 10% P95 or > 20% P99 vs baseline must be triaged and fixed or formally approved by runtime owners.
- Benchmark CI artifacts: CSV of samples, profiler outputs, trace bundle, and a short markdown summary. Store under s3://redwood-benchmarks/<release>/ with metadata.json containing run_provenance.

Ownership and maintenance
-------------------------
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime / benchmarking team. Contact: priya.kapoor@redwood.com
- Secondary reviewer: runtime-kernel team.
- Quarterly maintenance tasks: update representative models, add new hardware SKUs, rotate random seeds for replay freshness.

Appendix A - Example benchmark config (text)
------------------------------------------
{'name': 'short-chat-interactive', 'model': 'gpt-small-quant8-v2', 'hardware': 'A10G', 'duration_s': 600, 'rps': 12, 'sequence_length': 32, 'seed': 4832, 'provenance': {'model_sha': 'f9b8...', 'runtime_image': 'benchmark-runner:2027-02'}}

Appendix B - CLI cheatsheet
--------------------------
- Run locally: ./tools/benchmark-runner --config ./configs/short-chat.json --trace-id manual-001
- Upload artifacts: ./tools/benchmark-uploader --run-id manual-001 --bucket redwood-benchmarks --release 2027-02
- Compare to baseline: ./tools/bench-compare --current ./artifacts/manual-001/stats.csv --baseline s3://redwood-benchmarks/baseline/stats.csv --report out/report-manual-001.md

Appendix C - Change log
----------------------
- 2026-11-12 (created) - initial blueprint and catalog.
- 2027-02-18 (updated) - added mixed-tenant scenario and explicit provenance rules; tightened alert thresholds for short-chat.

Related artifacts and links
--------------------------
- Microbenchmark generator repo: infra/benchmark-generator
- Trace collection playbook: eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/continuous-runtime-profiling-strategy-2026
- Scheduler policy reference: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/scheduler-policy-language-declarative-profiles-2026

If you plan to add a new scenario, follow the SLO -> Benchmark mapping section and register the scenario in the canonical catalog at s3://redwood-benchmarks/catalog.json. For questions or to schedule runs on dedicated capacity, contact the owners listed above.
